title: THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE
text:

No record has been found of the teachers who carried on the school for the first two years after the fire, but the citizens apparently did not give up hope of re-establishing a private college, according to the following statement by Mr. L. G. Gee:

In 1892 I went to Anson in search of a school. While there I met Mr. W. B. Halsell. He told me then that the citizens of Savoy wanted him to return there to try to rebuild Savoy College, and that if he would come back to Savoy he could have the headship of it for five years. He persuaded me to join him in this enterprise. Halsell took the principalship, and I was employed as an assistant in mathematics and history.

Mr. Halsell, with Mr. Gee, did return to Savoy, but after two years Mr. Halsell moved to Durant, Indian Territory. Mr. Gee stayed and carried on. A pamphlet for 1897-98 reveals the following designations of teachers: L. G. Gee, principal and teacher of ancient languages and Bible; Professor H. A. Henderson, natural science (former F.A.M.E. teacher), mathematics and history; W. E. McMahan (also a former college teacher), Latin, physics, and chemistry; and Miss Martha Buford (likewise a Savoy College ex-student), primary. Mr. S. I. Chesworth, a Savoy graduate who married Miss Frankie Chesworth (graduate and former piano teacher of the College, a daughter of Mr. J. W. Chesworth, one of the founders), was principal of the school for the next several years.

Although the institution was evidently operated as a public school during these years, it seems to have carried the name of Savoy College, for in the report of the United States Commissioner of Education for 1897-1898 (the only year in which the Savoy school was reported) the name "Savoy College" appears in the statistical tabulations of high schools.
